summary: Transport-level queueing from client SDK connection reuse + aggressive retry policy causing perceived inference timeouts for high-throughput tenant
description:
Issue summary:
QuantisLabs reports a sudden increase in end-user perceived inference timeouts and long tail latency spikes starting 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Customer is on Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. They observe that a subset (~5%) of requests experience 10–30s 'hang' on the client before either timing out or finally receiving a response. Server-side metrics show healthy request completion in the same time window for most traffic, but client-side traces show queuing and repeated retry attempts.

Impact:
- High error/timeout rate for customer (approx 4% 504/timeouts) on peak traffic windows.
- Customer-facing end-to-end latency increase and SLO violations for their product.

Environment:
- Customer: QuantisLabs (dedicated plan)
- Region: prod us-east-1
- Redwood models: rw-13b-v2 (default), fallback rw-7b-instruct
- Client: QuantisLabs internal SDK v1.4.2 (NodeJS, http/2 enabled)
- Connection mode: SDK configured with connection pool size 2 and aggressive retry/backoff policy (maxRetries=5, initialBackoffMs=100, backoffMultiplier=2)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run sustained concurrent workload of 1k rps with 60 concurrent clients using SDK v1.4.2 against Redwood hosted endpoint.
2) Observe end-to-end latencies on the client side and count of request attempts per RPC.
3) Notice a small percent of requests receive 6–10 retry attempts and report client-side queueing prior to TCP/HTTP request dispatch.

Relevant logs/snippets from customer:
- Client-side trace: "[2026-03-09T21:15:02.112Z] request queued (pool wait=230ms), attempt=2"
- Server access logs: request completed in 180ms (same correlation id)
- SDK telemetry: persistent connection occupancy at 100% with backlog size fluctuating between 12-48 requests

Why we think this is happening (high level):
- Customer's SDK is reusing a very small number of underlying HTTP/2 streams/connections while generating bursts of parallel requests. When in-use connections hit their stream concurrency/window limits the SDK implementation falls back to queueing requests locally. Combined with an aggressive retry policy the client triggers cascades of queued requests which then release in waves, causing spikes in perceived latency and duplicate attempts.

Requested outcome:
- Short-term: reduce customer timeouts and mitigate user impact (possible client-side config guidance).
- Long-term: detect and surface this class of queuing via SDK telemetry and add guardrails in default retry/backoff settings or server-side SLO-aware throttling.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10: Triage call with QuantisLabs, SRE, and SDK team. Collected client SDK config and traces.
2026-03-10: Reproduced locally using internal load generator + customer SDK config. Observed queue depth on client side increase when concurrent in-flight requests per connection > 8 (http/2 stream/window interactions).
2026-03-11: Correlated spikes with times when customer's traffic pattern changed to many small messages (short prompts) causing higher QPS per client instance. Server-side CPU/GPU utilization remained normal; no serving-runtime timeouts found.
2026-03-12: SDK team instrumented connection pool metrics; observed pooling misconfiguration: poolSize=2 for ~50 concurrent worker threads. Also found retry policy allowed immediate re-enqueue of requests which amplified queueing.
Hypothesis: small poolSize + http/2 stream limits + retry re-enqueue logic created amplification under bursty workloads.
Diagnostic artifacts: client traces, SDK telemetry dump, access logs, small reproduce load script attached in linked PR.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Lina Cho (Support): Logged and acknowledged with QuantisLabs. Requested SDK config and traces.

2026-03-10 | Devon Carter (SRE): Confirmed reproduce locally with load tool. Seeing client queueing prior to egress (matches customer traces). Suspect poolSize too small and retry policy too aggressive.

2026-03-11 | Mateo Alvarez (SDK Eng): Implemented extra telemetry around http/2 stream occupancy and published a debug build for customer to test. Noted that Node http2 + keepalive semantics vary by platform--we should not assume unlimited concurrent streams per connection.
2026-03-11 | QuantisLabs (Customer): Tested debug build; reported 60% reduction in long-tail timeouts when increasing poolSize to 12 and reducing maxRetries to 2.
2026-03-12 | Ava Martinez (Support): Requested formal rollback/config guidance and recommended default SDK changes. Opened INT-4021 to track platform-side guardrails and telemetry improvements.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied and validated: customer increased SDK connection pool to 12 and lowered maxRetries to 2. Immediate customer impact reduced (long-tail timeouts down ~60%).
Short-term ops: Support provided step-by-step config changes and a patched debug SDK build.
Long-term plan: SDK team to propose default retry/backoff and pool sizing guidance (PR #1254). Platform team to add server-side telemetry alerts when per-tenant request queueing on ingress is detected. See linked INT-4021 for implementation track.
suggested_next_steps: Publish SDK guidance doc for pool sizing and retry configuration for high QPS workloads.
Merge PR #1254 to add http/2 stream occupancy telemetry and new default retry/backoff in SDK v1.5.0.
Add an alert runbook to Console for per-tenant request queue depth and abnormal retry amplification.
Follow up with QuantisLabs in 72 hours to verify stability under peak load.
